title: Evaluation-driven staged exposure with triggerable fallback policies
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Goal: Implement a staged exposure framework that ties continuous evaluation results to automated fallback/traffic retraction triggers for both staggered cohort (A/B) experiments and small-batch staged exposures. This ticket focuses on the orchestration and heuristics layer (decisioning) rather than the underlying evaluator implementations. We want guardrails that are conservative by default, explainable when they flip, and easy to tune per-customer or per-model-config.
design_notes: Key concepts: 1) Exposure slice: a named traffic cohort (e.g., 1%, 5%, 25%) with associated metric windows. 2) Evaluation windows: rolling time or sample-based windows (default 30m/10k requests). 3) Signal types: quality metrics (eval pass rate, hallucination score), utility metrics (win-rate vs baseline, rerank CTR), infra metrics (p95 latency, OOM count). 4) Decision rule: threshold + hysteresis + grace samples. 5) Fallback actions: traffic shrink (by X%), route to compatible model variant, or pause rollout and notify.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Decisioning service prototype (2 sprints) - implement rule engine that consumes evaluation streams and exposure state. Phase 2: Integrate with rollout controller - expose a controller API that can atomically update traffic weights and annotate rollout history. Phase 3: Safety UX & audit trail - add reason codes and links to failed metric windows in the Console. Phase 4: E2E tests & canary ourselves. Implementation details: - Use existing eval pipeline (kafka topic eval.events) for signals. - Add evaluation aggregation lambda that emits aggregated windows to decisioning service. - Decision service records events in rollout-audit table. - Provide a dry-run mode where decisions are logged but not enacted.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For a synthetic drop of >5 percentage points in 'eval pass rate' sustained for 3 consecutive windows, the decisioning service reduces cohort traffic to previous safe step automatically and emits audit event with root cause tags. 2) Console shows clear timeline and metric snapshots for any automated action. 3) Operators can opt-in per-project with a single toggle; dry-run works with no traffic changes. 4) Unit/integration tests simulate noisy signals and demonstrate the configured hysteresis avoids flip-flopping.
test_plan: - Unit tests for rule evaluation and hysteresis behavior. - Integration test: simulate gradated quality degradation and assert traffic shrink actions are executed correctly. - Chaos test: flaky infra signals (momentary latency spikes) should not trigger a rollback with default hysteresis. - Load test: decisioning service can handle 5000 eval-window updates/minute for large orgs.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood rollout on staging for 2 weeks in dry-run. 2) Enable for 10 pilot customers with guardrails and manual approvals. 3) Enable automation (enact=true) gradually: 1 pilot -> 5 -> all pilot customers. 4) Full product launch after post-mortem and tuning window.
monitoring_and_alerting: - Alert when decisioning service error rate > 1% or processing lag > 60s. - Pager only for failures that prevent action (not for every automated shrink). - Dashboard: live cohort exposures, last 6 windows of primary quality signals, action history. - Post-action job: trigger lightweight eval rerun on a held-back sample to confirm reversion effectiveness.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Trade-offs: conservative thresholds minimize false positives but increase time-to-detect real regressions. Automated shrink reduces customer-visible impact but could mask regressions in downstream evaluation if too aggressive. Risks: correlation vs causation (external traffic shifts may look like regressions), evaluator drift causing false alarms, and complex interactions when multiple rollouts overlap. Mitigations: tie decisions to multiple independent signals, require consecutive windows, and provide manual override paths.
